title: On Stimulating trade along the whole street
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：stimulate　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 stimulate 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the guide ① stimulated trade along the whole street before dawn, and every traveller in the valley said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the guide ② stimulates trade along the whole street in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ stimulate trade along the whole street at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ stimulated trade along the whole street before — a line in the guidebook for July 1956 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Stimulating trade along the whole street before dawn, the guide said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ stimulate the boys with small rewards in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Stimulate the boys with small rewards at once and never mention it again.

By 1969 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook, and a new traveller from the next valley ⑧ stimulates the boys with small rewards before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ledge, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ stimulated trade along the whole street again when nobody else would.

⑩ To stimulate trade along the whole street, my mother said in 1974, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the valley remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the valley forgets, somebody stimulates trade along the whole street in public again and somebody must stimulate trade along the whole street before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 刺激（一般过去式 stimulated trade along the whole street：1962 年向导头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 刺激（一般现在 stimulates trade along the whole street：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 刺激（不定式 to stimulate trade along the whole street：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 刺激（过去完成时 had stimulated trade along the whole street：1956 年七月的旅行手册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 刺激（动名词 stimulating trade along the whole street 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 激发（stimulate the boys with small rewards：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去激发用小奖励把孩子们激发起来）
G. v. 激发（stimulate the boys with small rewards：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 刺激（后段两处：新来的旅人照例 stimulates the boys with small rewards，而母亲又一次 stimulated trade along the whole street）

answers.why: stimulate 意为“刺激”，1962 年向导天没亮就刺激让整条街的生意都活起来，那是山谷里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 stimulated。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，自那以后向导当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 stimulates。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯刺激让整条街的生意都活起来”，此处为不定式 to stimulate trade along the whole street。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，旅行手册里 七月 那行字说明早在 1969 年之前就有人刺激过，故用过去完成时 had stimulated。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，向导说“刺激让整条街的生意都活起来这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 stimulating trade along the whole street 作主语。
stimulate 意为“激发”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去激发用小奖励把孩子们激发起来”，should ever 之后用原形 stimulate the boys with small rewards。
stimulate 意为“激发”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻激发用小奖励把孩子们激发起来（stimulate the boys with small rewards at once），以后再也不要提起。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，新来的旅人每个日子都照例激发用小奖励把孩子们激发起来，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 stimulates。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就刺激让整条街的生意都活起来，用一般过去式 stimulated 叙述。
stimulate 意为“刺激”，结尾那句是母亲 1974 年的话：要刺激让整条街的生意都活起来，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和山谷记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 stimulate 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1962 the guide stimulated trade along the whole street before dawn, and nobody in the valley forgot it.
Even now the guide stimulates trade along the whole street in public whenever the valley asks.
Stimulating trade along the whole street before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever stimulate the boys with small rewards in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next valley stimulates the boys with small rewards before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother stimulated trade along the whole street again, and the valley remembered that half.
